findings.title: Negative resource units invent phantom capacity and clear crane overallocation
findings.description: add_activity() accepts any float in resource_requirements, including negatives. calculate_resource_profile() and identify_overallocations() sum assignment.units with no units>0 check. A phantom activity with CRANE=-1 on the same days as two 1-crane steel picks cancels the overload: overallocations become {} and peak_usage falls to capacity while both picks remain scheduled.
findings.impact: Official resource histograms and leveling report a single tower crane as feasible for simultaneous steel picks — struck-by / collapse planning failure and hidden overallocation.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses ResourceOptimizer as the live crane/crew loading authority.
2. Two critical steel activities each require CRANE:1 on the same days (capacity=1) → overallocation detected.
3. Attacker adds a phantom activity with resource_requirements={'CRANE': -1} overlapping those days (is_critical=True so leveling will not shift it away).
4. identify_overallocations() returns {}; peak_usage=1.0; make-ready publishes a clean crane plan.
findings.remediation: Require units > 0 on add_activity assignments. Reject unknown resource_ids. Treat negative demand as an error, not a credit against capacity.
findings.poc_video_notes: Local PoC: before phantom CRANE over=+1 for 5 days; after CRANE:-1 → overallocations={}, peak=1.0.

findings.title: crash_cost < normal_cost yields negative crash_slope so compression plans report negative cost (paid to accelerate)
findings.description: Activity.crash_slope = (crash_cost - normal_cost) / (normal_duration - crash_duration) with no requirement that crash_cost >= normal_cost. analyze_crash_options sorts by ascending slope, so a zero/negative crash_cost activity is preferred. crash_schedule adds that negative slope into total_additional_cost each day. Distinct from the already-reported phantom achieved_reduction when parallel critical paths keep CPM duration unchanged: this invents negative dollars on the CompressionPlan even when duration does drop.
findings.impact: Official compression / time-cost curve publishes accelerating the job as a profit (e.g. -$50k for 5 crash days). Buyout and recovery decisions treat that forged savings as real.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent builds a crash/fast-track recovery plan via ScheduleCompressor.
2. Attacker supplies Foundation with normal_cost=$100k and crash_cost=$0 (or negative).
3. crash_slope = -$10k/day; crash_schedule(5) selects it first.
4. CompressionPlan.total_additional_cost = -$50,000 with achieved_reduction=5 is published as the recovery option.
findings.remediation: Require crash_cost >= normal_cost and crash_duration < normal_duration with positive durations. Reject non-positive crash slopes. Cap total_additional_cost at >= 0 unless an authenticated VE credit is recorded separately.
findings.poc_video_notes: Local PoC: Foundation crash_cost=0 → slope=-10000; crash 5 days → total_additional_cost=-50000.

findings.title: Zero or negative activity duration collapses CPM project length (90d→50d/40d)
findings.description: import_schedule/add_activity accept duration without requiring duration > 0. _forward_pass sets early_finish = early_start + duration, so duration=0 removes a 40-day steel activity from the path length and duration=-10 pulls successors earlier. Distinct from the already-reported predecessor-cycle → empty forward-pass / duration=0 finding: this is an acyclic network with attacker-controlled non-positive durations.
findings.impact: Official CPM reports a 40–50 day project instead of 90 days. Float, critical path, and delay simulation all trust the collapsed length — hidden steel schedule risk and false recovery.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent runs CriticalPathAnalyzer as the live CPM / delay-impact tool.
2. Attacker imports Found(30)→Steel(0 or -10)→Roof(20) instead of Steel(40).
3. calculate_critical_path() yields project_duration 50 (zero) or 40 (negative) vs honest 90.
4. Downstream look-ahead and LD analysis consume the collapsed duration.
findings.remediation: Reject duration <= 0 on import/add. Fail closed before forward/backward pass if any activity has non-positive duration.
findings.poc_video_notes: Local PoC: honest 90d; Steel duration=0 → 50d; Steel duration=-10 → 40d.

findings.title: record_ncr_response accepts negative cost_impact/schedule_impact and publishes inverted QC liability
findings.description: record_ncr_response stores caller cost_impact and schedule_impact with no sign or magnitude checks, then stamps NCRStatus.ACCEPTED. get_quality_metrics / generate_qc_report sum those fields across all NCRs. Distinct from the already-reported NCR auto-ACCEPT / verify_remediation evidence skip: this is the negative-value integrity bug on official cost/schedule impact totals (even a single accepted NCR with cost_impact=-500000 drives total_cost_impact negative).
findings.impact: QC dashboards and owner reports can show negative cost and schedule impact for real CRITICAL defects — understating liability and recovery exposure.
findings.attack_path:
1. Agent uses QualityControlManager as the NCR / QC metrics system of record.
2. A CRITICAL defect NCR is created (or already exists).
3. Attacker calls record_ncr_response(..., cost_impact=-500000, schedule_impact=-30).
4. get_quality_metrics and generate_qc_report publish total_cost_impact=-500000 and -30 schedule days.
findings.remediation: Require cost_impact >= 0 and schedule_impact_days >= 0 (or a separate authenticated credit path). Cap magnitudes; do not auto-ACCEPT on response.
findings.poc_video_notes: Local PoC: record_ncr_response cost_impact=-500000 schedule_impact=-30 → metrics totals match; report includes $-500,000.
